findings.claim: The change does not fix the crash in the repro. The repro's `Item<T>` and `Cmd` put `[Key]` on every member, so neither patched diagnostic (BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull, MemberNeedsKey) is ever created for them; those two sites cannot be what throws. When `reportDiagnostic` is null, `this.reportDiagnostic?.Invoke(...)` skips evaluating its arguments, so any indexing inside those calls never runs. The first unguarded `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` the reporter named (issue line 735, about base line 711 given the consistent 24-line offset to the two patched sites) has no hunk. The `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` wrapper filters diagnostics only after `Diagnostic.Create`'s arguments have run, so it cannot stop an index exception. A closed generic struct or record struct from a metadata reference most likely still throws IndexOutOfRangeException in the generator (CS8785, no resolver) and the analyzer (AD0001).

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ClosedGenericStructFromMetadataTests. It compiles `lib` (generic record struct and generic struct) to a PE image, references it from `app` exactly as in REQ-2283, then runs MessagePackGenerator through CSharpGeneratorDriver and MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer through CompilationWithAnalyzers. It asserts there is no generator exception, no CS8785, no analyzer exception and no AD0001.

findings.claim: `MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth` was raised from 500 to 5000. This is unrelated to REQ-2283 and weakens the secure-by-default untrusted-data profile. Attacker-controlled payloads can now nest 10x deeper before rejection, which brings back stack-exhaustion risk (an uncatchable StackOverflowException in .NET) that the 500 limit was there to prevent (ledger L9 records the 500 depth limit).

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.UntrustedDataDepthLimitTests.UntrustedData_MaximumObjectGraphDepth_Is500. It asserts MessagePackSecurity.UntrustedData.MaximumObjectGraphDepth == 500 and fails on head (5000).

findings.claim: The new wrapper drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not in source, including Location.None. `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` uses `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, so a source-declared positional record property (its declaring syntax is a ParameterSyntax) gets a null location. Example: `[MessagePackObject] public record R([property: Key(null)] string A);` in the compiling assembly. That property's BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull error is now silently dropped by `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation`, even though the offending symbol is in this compilation. The same applies to any other diagnostic created with a null location for a source symbol: it is now dropped where it was reported before.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the analyzer (CompilationWithAnalyzers with MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer, LanguageVersion.Latest) on a source record `[MessagePackObject] public record R([property: Key(null)] string A);`. Assert that a diagnostic with descriptor MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull is reported. On head none is reported, because the null location is filtered out.
